claims.summary: For M >= 2, 1 <= p <= M-1, k = M-p, N = 2M-p, t >= 1, and L_t the cherry window with its top column raised by t: the least coefficient of P_(L_t) is Vand^2 tau^(t), tau^(t) = c_(M,p) (c_(N-1+t)/c_(N-1)) N sum_(b<=t) alpha_b H_(b), H_(b) = sum_(|S|=k+1) Vand(y_S)^2 h_b(y_S), alpha_b = sum_(s=b..t) h_(t-s)(y) V[b,s], V the inverse of the upper triangular U with U[r,r] = N+r, U[r,q] = p_(q-r); alpha_t = 1/(N+t). Hence where H_(0) = ... = H_(t-1) = 0 (e.g. t = 2 on Sigma_k), tau^(t) is a nonzero constant times H_(t).
claims.assessment: Working proof (the top-up proof with eliminator z^(k-1) h P, h the polynomial part of z^(M+t)/P, Jacobi's complementary minor expanded along the staircase rows, Cauchy-Binet with Jacobi-Trudi); exact check 30/30 for M = 3, 4, every p, t <= 3 (research/results/bmd-20261009-ket/single-shift.txt); reviewed by one fresh-context medium reviewer.
claims.rationale: Gives the top-shift coefficients the Hankel criterion review asked for, as a triangular Schur-Hankel hierarchy deciding the residual Sigma_k level by level.
